newsitem.title: USA: Grand Prix sets two races events in Memphis.
newsitem.headline: Grand Prix sets two races events in Memphis.

text.p: Grand Prix Association of Long Beach, owner and operator of auto racing tracks and races, on Monday said two major auto racing groups have scheduled 1997 events at its Memphis Motorsports Park.
The races, the Automobile Racing Club of America's (ARCA) Super Car and United States Auto Club's (USAC) Silver Crown series events are slated for September 12-14.
The company is starting a $2.5 million renovation and expansion at the track to produce a new nine-tenths mile paved oval with seating for 25,000.

"We are negotiating with other major race sanctioning organizations to add our new Memphis facility to their event calendars, and we are confident that we will host a full schedule of events on our new oval in 1998," Christopher Pook, chief executive officer said in a statement.

The ARCA Super Car stock car series and the USAC Silver Crown open-wheel series are two of the longest running race circuits in North America. They will be the first major series hosted at the renovated Memphis facility.

In June, Grand Prix raised $11.9 million through a public offering to fund its acquisition and expansion of permanent racing venues, thus providing year-round revenues to augment the company's Toyota Grand Prix of Long Beach each spring.
